intro: Every counter on the home page is a claim, and a claim needs a definition: what exactly is counted, what is excluded, and when the number was last true. This page is that definition. When a number changes, the change lands here first, dated.

counters.label: Hours spent
counters.counts: Working hours spent on the BYKO study since 2 Aug 2026: contract work, liquidity setup, the website, listing applications, wallet-flag appeals, support conversations, and writing. Tracked per session, rounded to the half hour. Self-reported estimate from the project diary; it will increase as the remaining episodes get logged.
counters.excludes: Thinking about BYKO in the shower. Only sessions with an artifact — a commit, a submitted form, a sent message — are counted.

counters.label: Dollars spent
counters.counts: Direct out-of-pocket cost of the study: $74.02 is the exact, verified, irreversible pool-funding transaction; roughly $10 is estimated micro-buy activity, gas and infrastructure. The budget is deliberately tiny — that is the point.
counters.excludes: The founder's own BYKO purchases from the pool (those are votes, not costs) and the value of the time counted in hours above.

counters.label: Listing rejections
counters.counts: Rejections counted per submission wave — a distinct submission date, not a distinct email: 04, 05 and 11 Aug 2026 so far. One wave can answer with several template refusals the same day (one bundled four identical emails); it still counts once. A submission with no reply after the service's own stated review window also counts — silence is an answer.
counters.excludes: Forms never submitted, paid fast-track offers (declined on principle — see Paid listings), and resubmissions of the same form that are still inside the review window.

counters.label: Wallet flags
counters.counts: Wallet products that mark BYKO as risky or suspected spam by default, counted per product, verified by opening the token in the wallet and screenshotting the warning.
counters.excludes: Third-party allowlist databases the wallets read from — the flag is counted once, at the wallet where the user sees it.

counters.label: Flags removed
counters.counts: Warnings that a wallet or scanner has actually stopped showing, counted per warning at the product where a user sees it, verified by reopening the token there. So far one: MetaMask's "Low locked liquidity", dropped by Blockaid within about a day of the LP burn on 7 Aug 2026 — removed by evidence, with no email, form or appeal.
counters.excludes: Warnings still displayed ("Unstable price" in MetaMask, the Base app scam flag) and removals promised in a reply but not visible in the product — a flag counts only when the warning is gone from the screen.

counters.label: Paid listings
counters.counts: Listings, promotions or fast-track reviews paid for with money. The study's rule is that this number stays zero; if it ever changes, the diary explains why in full.
